question.explanation:
First, recall that:

\begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0}\mathbf f(s) & = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} \left(s^2+6\right) \\ \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{s}{s-10} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} e^{5s} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

  • For the first component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0} \left(s^2+6\right) &= 0^2+6 = 6 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

  • For the second component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{s}{s-10} &= \dfrac{0}{0-10} = 0 \end{align*}

  • For the third component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0} e^{5s} &= e^{5(0)} =1 \end{align*}

Hence, $ \lim\limits_{s \to 0}\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, the limit of $\left\| \mathbf f(s) \right\|$ as $s$ approaches $0$ is: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0} \left\|\mathbf f(s) \right\| & = \left\| \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0}\mathbf f(s) \right\| \\[3pt] & = \left\| \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \right\| \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{6^2+0^2+1^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{37} \end{align*}

question.text:
Find the limit $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 3} \big[\mathbf f(t) \cdot \mathbf g(t)\big]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as:

\begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) & = \sqrt t \,\mathbf i + \ln (t-2)\, \mathbf j + t\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] \mathbf g(t) & = \ln(t-2) \,\mathbf i + \dfrac {t-t^2}{1-t}\, \mathbf j + 2\, \mathbf k \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function:

\begin{align} \lim_{t \to 3} \mathbf f(t) & = \left( \lim_{t \to 3} \sqrt t\right) \,\mathbf i + \left( \lim_{t \to 3} \ln (t-2)\right)\, \mathbf j + \left(\lim_{t \to 3} t \right)\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] & = \sqrt 3 \,\mathbf i + \ln(3-2)\, \mathbf j + 3\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] & = \sqrt 3 \,\mathbf i + 0\, \mathbf j + 3\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] & = \sqrt 3 \,\mathbf i + 3\, \mathbf k \\[5pt] \lim_{t \to 3} \mathbf g(t) & = \left( \lim_{t \to 3} \ln(t-2)\right) \,\mathbf i +\left( \lim_{t \to 3} \dfrac {t-t^2}{1-t}\right)\, \mathbf j + \left(\lim_{t \to 3} 2\right)\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] & = \left(\lim_{t \to 3} \ln(t-2)\right) \,\mathbf i + \left(\lim_{t \to 3} \dfrac {t(1-t)}{1-t}\right)\, \mathbf j +\left( \lim_{t \to 3} 2\right)\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] & = \left(\lim_{t \to 3} \ln(t-2)\right) \,\mathbf i +\left( \lim_{t \to 3} t\right)\, \mathbf j + \left( \lim_{t \to 3} 2\right)\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] & = \ln(3-2) \,\mathbf i + 3\, \mathbf j + 2\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] & = 0 \,\mathbf i + 3\, \mathbf j + 2\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] & = 3\, \mathbf j + 2\, \mathbf k \end{align}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align} \lim_{t \to 3} \big[ \mathbf f(t) \cdot \mathbf g(t) \big] & =\lim_{t \to 3}\mathbf f(t) \cdot \lim_{t \to 3}\mathbf g(t) \\[3pt] & = \left( \sqrt 3 \,\mathbf i + 3\, \mathbf k \right) \cdot \left(3\, \mathbf j + 2\, \mathbf k \right) \\[3pt] & = {\sqrt 3 \cdot 0 + 0 \cdot 3 + 3 \cdot 2} \\[3pt] & = 6. \end{align}

question.text:
Find $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \big[ \mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t) \big]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as:

\begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 2e^t \\ \dfrac{1-\cos t}{t} \\ \dfrac{t^2+4}{t-2} \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf g(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 2t-2 \\ \dfrac{4t-1}{t^2-1} \\ 4^t \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of $\mathbf f(t)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} 2e^t \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{1-\cos t}{t} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{t^2+4}{t-2} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2e^0 \\ 0 \\ \dfrac{0^2+4}{0-2} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}\\[7pt] \end{align*}

The limit of a second component here was found using L'Hopital's Rule: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{1-\cos t}t &= \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{(1-\cos t)'}{t'} \\[3pt] &= \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{\sin t}{1} \\[3pt] &= \dfrac{\sin 0}{1} \\[3pt] &= 0 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

Now, we find the limit of $\mathbf g(t)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} (2t - 2) \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{4t-1}{t^2-1} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} 4^t \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2(0)-2 \\ \dfrac{4(0)-1}{0^2-1} \\ 4^0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \big[ \mathbf f(t) + 2\mathbf g(t) \big] & = \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) + 2 \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) \\[3pt] & = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} + 2 \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[3pt] & = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} \\[3pt] & = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Limit of a Sum of Vector Functions

question.explanation:
First, recall that:

\begin{align*} \lim_{s \to1}\mathbf f(s) & = \left \langle \lim_{s \to 1}\dfrac{\ln{s^2}}{s-1}, \: \lim_{s \to 1} \dfrac{6s-\sin{(s-1)}}{3s-2}, \: \lim_{s \to 1} \dfrac{s^3+4s-2}{s^2+s-1} \right \rangle \end{align*}

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

  • The first component can be found using L'Hopital's Rule: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{\ln{s^2}}{s-1} &= \lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{2\ln{s}}{s-1} \\[3pt] &=\lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{(2\ln{s})'}{(s-1)'} \\[3pt] &= \lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{2}{s}\right)}{1} \\[3pt] &= 2 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

  • For the second component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 1} \dfrac{6s-\sin{(s-1)}}{3s-2} &= \dfrac{6(1)-\sin{(1-1)}}{3(1)-2}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{6-0}{1}\\[5pt] &=6 \end{align*}

  • For the third component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 1} \dfrac{s^3+4s-2}{s^2+s-1} &= \dfrac{(1)^3+4(1)-2}{(1)^2+(1)-1}\\[3pt] &= \dfrac{3}{1}\\[3pt] &= 3 \end{align*}

Hence, $ \lim\limits_{s \to 1}\mathbf f(s) = \left\langle 2, \: 6, \: 3 \right\rangle.$

Finally, the limit of $\left\| \mathbf f(s) \right\|$ as $s$ approaches $1$ is \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 1} \left\|\mathbf f(s) \right\| & = \left\| \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 1}\mathbf f(s) \right\| \\[3pt] & = \left\| \left\langle 2, \: 6, \: 3 \right\rangle \right\| \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{2^2+6^2 +3^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{4+36+9} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{49} \\[3pt] &= 7 . \end{align*}

question.text: Find $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} [\mathbf f(t) - 2\mathbf g(t)]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as \begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) & = \left\langle 1+\sin t, \, t^2-1 , \, \dfrac {4+t} {2-t^2} \right\rangle ,\\[5pt] \mathbf g(t) & = \left\langle \cos t, \, \dfrac{1}{2}, \, \sqrt t + \sqrt 3 \right\rangle. \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function: \begin{align} \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 0} \, (1+\sin t), \, \lim_{t \to 0} \, (t^2-1) , \, \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{4+t}{2-t^2} \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle 1+\sin 0, 0^2-1 , \dfrac {4+0} {2-0^2} \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle 1, -1 , 2 \right\rangle\\[5pt] \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 0} \cos{t}, \, \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{1}{2}, \, \lim_{t \to 0} \, (\sqrt t + \sqrt 3) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \cos 0, \dfrac{1}{2},\sqrt 0 + \sqrt 3\right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 1, \dfrac{1}{2}, \sqrt{3} \right\rangle \end{align}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align} \lim_{t \to 0} [\mathbf f(t) - 2\mathbf g(t)]& = \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) - \lim_{t \to 0} 2\mathbf g(t) \\[5pt] & = \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) - 2\lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 1, -1, 2 \right\rangle - 2\left\langle 1, \dfrac{1}{2},\sqrt{3} \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle 1, -1 , 2 \right\rangle - \left\langle 2, 1,2\sqrt 3 \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle 1-2, -1-1,2-2\sqrt 3 \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle -1,-2,2-2\sqrt{3} \right\rangle \end{align}
